subject: Welcome to the biogeobears google group!

messages.subject: Welcome to the biogeobears google group!
parts:
To interested biogeographers,

For my Ph.D., I created the R package "BioGeoBEARS" in order
to allow statistical comparison and testing of various
phylogenetic models in historical biogeography.

This has already attracted dozens of users, and along with
that, questions. I am happy to answer these privately, but
it is more useful to the community at large if
questions/answers are posted to a public listserv searchable
by google. I encourage people to not be shy, and to post
their questions publicly.

There is no such thing as a dumb question, especially in a
language like R, where hard things are sometimes easy, and
easy things are sometimes hard! I like people to be nice on
my lists, so if anyone violates the "be nice" rule I will
ask them to take this off-list, or bump them off the list in
extreme situations.

USES OF THE LIST:

- ask/answer questions about BioGeoBEARS

- announcements about BioGeoBEARS updates/new features/bug fixes

- bug reports

- feature requests (which I will address as time allows;
sometimes something is easy, sometimes hard!)

- announcements of pertinent posters/talks/meetings/grants

- historical biogeography discussion, but focused
specifically on improving the probablistic models used in
BioGeoBEARS. I am not up for extended philosophical battles
about dispersal vs. vicariance, cladistics, panbiogeography,
Hennig being a Nazi, etc., which I have sometimes seen take
over online discussions. There are other lists for that.
The BioGeoBEARS method, and this list, should be focused on
probablistic, statistical inference, and the practicals of that.

Thanks, and cheers!

Nick Matzke
2013-10-01
